subject: Feasibility: ClearRiver private (VPC / on-prem) — architecture & resourcing questions
messages:

Subject: Feasibility: ClearRiver private (VPC / on-prem) — architecture & resourcing questions

Team —

Following the call with ClearRiver yesterday, they want us to sketch an actionable feasibility response for a private deployment option (VPC peering + optional on-site appliance). High-level asks they reiterated:

- VPC peering across their AWS account with strict ingress controls (no public endpoints)
- Option for on-prem appliance in a locked rack (air-gapped-ish) for PHI workflows
- SSO via SAML, SCIM provisioning, and detailed audit logs (7 years retention might be requested)
- Encryption keys under the customer KMS (HSM integration preferred)

They want a short summary of architecture options and a recommended pilot plan by EOD Thursday so procurement can start the paperwork. I attached the draft network diagram and a starter SOW (stubs) — please review and annotate: network-design-v2.pdf, sow-draft.docx.

Primary questions I need input on from each of you:

- Karthik: technical constraints we should call out (latency, KV cache persistence, model variant compatibility, whether we can support their air-gap/upgrade process).
- Jonas: rough resourcing + timeline for a 6–12 week pilot, plus any SLAs we can realistically promise for a reserved pilot cluster.
- Marissa: product gating items — control plane placement (hosted vs private control plane), licensing terms we need to add to SOW.

Keep replies inline so I can compile. If anything looks like a hard no, flag it explicitly.

Thanks —
Stephanie
Sr. Product Lead, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Feasibility: ClearRiver private (VPC / on-prem) — architecture & resourcing questions

Stephanie — quick technical notes based on the diagram and their constraints. TL;DR: feasible but with nontrivial integration work and a few permanent limitations to call out.

Key points:
- Network: VPC peering is workable for AWS-to-AWS traffic, but if they want isolated on-prem with no internet egress we need to support a site-to-site VPN or Direct Connect. Direct Connect is preferred for production (stable latency + bandwidth).
- Control plane: we can run a private control plane (customer-hosted) but that increases ops burden and removes some automatic rollout features. Recommended: private control plane deployed in their account, with our agents running in an isolated subnet.
- KV / cache: persistent KV cache on customer-managed NVMe is possible but we must encrypt all secrets and provide clear backup/restore runbooks. Cold-start latency for large context models will be higher unless we pre-warm tokens — call this out.
- Model variants / quantization: we can support standard quantized weights but air-gapped on-prem will require a signed-asset transfer process and a manual install flow. We should not promise automated zero-touch upgrades.
- Identity + keys: SAML + SCIM is fine. For customer KMS, we can integrate with AWS KMS or customer HSM via PKCS11 but that will add ~2–4 engineering sprints for cert handling and rotation automation.
- Monitoring / logs: we can stream audit logs to their SIEM (S3 / Splunk / SQS). Retention for 7 years will be an ops + storage cost to quantify.

Open technical unknowns (need answers from ClearRiver):
1) Do they require fully air-gapped installs (no outbound) or just private VPC with egress control?
2) Expected RPS and peak token/sec for pilot workloads?
3) On-prem hardware spec — GPU count + networking (10/25/100Gb)?

I can draft a short appendix for the SOW that captures these limits. If we go private control plane, we should budget for 2 engineers (1 infra, 1 runtime) full-time during pilot plus 0.5 oncall afterwards.

-Karthik
Engineering Manager, Runtime
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Feasibility: ClearRiver private (VPC / on-prem) — architecture & resourcing questions

Thanks — adding resource and timeline perspective.

Assuming we accept the private control-plane + optional on-prem appliance approach, here is a conservative pilot plan:

Pilot scope (6–8 weeks):
- Week 0–1: agreement on network topology, sign SOW, handshake on procurement window.
- Week 2–3: infra provisioning (Direct Connect + VPC peering), customer account setup, control plane deployment in customer account (minimal config).
- Week 4–5: model packaging + secure asset transfer, runbook validation, smoke tests with 50% expected production traffic.
- Week 6–8: stabilization, runbook handoff, 2-week validation window.

Estimated resourcing (pilot):
- 2 FTE engineering (Karthik's runtime + 1 infra/ops) — full-time for 6–8 weeks
- 0.5 PM/Eng manager (Stephanie) for coordination
- 0.5 Solutions engineer (Marissa) for SSO / procurement support
- 0.25 Legal / contracts support for SOW redlines

Cost buckets to flag for the customer / procurement:
- Dedicated infra (pilot cluster): hourly GPUs + storage — we should give a ballpark after we get expected load numbers.
- Professional services (setup + runbooks) — we should include a 6–8 week services line in SOW.
- Ongoing support add-on for private control plane (managed ops) — suggest offering Tiered support pricing.

Product callouts for SOW (Marissa):
- Must specify control plane placement (hosted vs customer-managed). If customer-managed, include clear limitations: no automatic canary, longer rollback windows, manual security patch flow.
- Define SLA for pilot (availability target) and fallback policy (fallback to hosted variant only for read-only queries, not PHI processing unless contractually approved).

I'll pull together a rough effort estimate spreadsheet and share by EOD.

Jonas
Head of Deployments
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Feasibility: ClearRiver private (VPC / on-prem) — architecture & resourcing questions

Stephanie, team — thanks for the quick turnaround. Helpful initial read. A few clarifications from our side that will help unblock procurement: 

- We require outbound egress to be blocked for PHI workloads. Non-PHI telemetry can be allowed to a restricted set of endpoints (security team will provide allowlist).
- For the on-prem appliance option, procurement needs a hardware spec and an installation window (we have onsite installers available July 26–Aug 2). Please let us know if Redwood can commit to that timeline for an initial install.
- Key management: we prefer customer-controlled KMS and need to see an integration plan (rotation + emergency key-eviction playbook).
- Regarding audit logs: 7-year retention is non-negotiable for now, but we are open to a tiered proposal (hot logs for 90 days, cold for long-term retention).

Procurement asked for a formal SOW and a one-page technical appendix describing the installation and data-flow. Can you send that by Thursday (7/2)? Also curious about rough cost estimate for the 6-week pilot once you have the effort spreadsheet.

Lydia Park
Director, Cloud Security
ClearRiver Health
